resale_co.name: Occupancy Certificate of Code Compliance (CCO, Certificate of Continued Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Holmdel Township Department of Community Development (Enforcement Officer; Code Enforcement and Bureau of Fire Prevention staff)
resale_co.lead_time: Submit the application and fees at least 10 business days before the new owner moves in. Inspections can be requested up to 30 days ahead and are scheduled in the order received. A CCO or denial is issued within 10 business days of a complete application; a reinspection is done within 3 business days of the request.
requirements: Property history review: all construction permits closed, all violations closed and penalties paid, deed and zoning restrictions checked
Work done without required construction permits is sent to the Construction Official and cited; the owner must obtain the permits

Exterior: accessory structures, walks and driveways in good repair; yard free of overgrowth and rubbish; wells and septic maintained or properly abandoned; pool gates self-closing and self-latching at least 54 inches high
Address numbers at least 3 inches high on the house or mailbox; exterior surfaces free of peeling paint and termite activity; stairs, decks and porches with approved handrails and guards

Interior: no second kitchen unless deed-restricted and permitted; no basement sleeping quarters without a permitted second exit; windows and doors working with screens; handrails on stairs with more than three risers; guards on landings 30 inches or higher

Bathroom exhaust fan or window; metal dryer duct vented outside; fuel-fired appliances properly vented; front door opens from inside without a key (no double-keyed deadbolts); sump pump not tied to the sanitary sewer; all utilities on
All parts of the premises must be accessible for the inspection

fees.label: CCO, sale of a single-family home, condominium or townhouse, initial inspection
Second and later reinspections, each (first reinspection free)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online for a Residential Certificate of Code Compliance through the Township's SDL Portal (link on the Occupancy Certificate page) and pay before the inspection is scheduled. Apply at least 10 business days before the closing or move-in. Download the Residential Occupancy Certificate Checklist to prepare.
resale_co.contact_title: Technical Assistant, Bureau of Fire Prevention / Community Development

evidence.quote: Such inspection is required to be conducted at the time a Residential or Commercial property is sold, leased, or rented, or when a Commercial occupancy moves into a new space.

A real estate agent licensee who is involved in the sale of any property must obtain or ensure that the seller obtains a Certificate of Code Compliance from the Department of Community Development prior to the sale, transfer of ownership or occupancy

No person, agency, corporation, partnership, firm, company, owner, real estate agent, broker or any other individual shall rent, lease, sell, occupy, transfer title of any dwelling, dwelling unit, commercial building or space, or property without first obtaining a CCO certificate from the Enforcement Officer.
Within 10 business days of receipt of a complete application, the Enforcement Officer or his designee shall issue either a CCO certificate or a CCO certificate denial.
Occupancy Type: Single-Family, Condominium, Townhouse (Sales Only)

resale_co.notes: Township code Chapter 20 (Residential and Commercial Property Regulations) was read through the ecode360 text reader. The sale fee in the code and both Township fee sheets covers a single-family home, condominium or townhouse; no separate sale fee for a two-family home is published (rental of an apartment in a two-family is $150). No validity period for a sale CCO was found. Staff on the Occupancy Certificate page: David Olsen, Fire Official (ext. 1315, dolsen@holmdel.gov); Dina Rosado, Technical Assistant (ext. 1307); Fire Prevention Specialists Darnell McDonald (ext. 1317), Shawn O'Connor (ext. 1321) and Adalberto Rodriguez (ext. 1319). Landlord registration and rental CCOs are rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19
Fire extinguisher (Township sheets still list it): the fee summary and workflow still call the certificate a smoke alarm, carbon monoxide alarm and portable fire extinguisher certificate (CSACMAPFEC)

fire_cert.notes: The two Township fee sheets (both last revised 3.12.2026) disagree. The workflow sheet lists $45 (more than four business days), $90 (four business days or less) and $161 (fewer than four business days), which overlap. The fee summary lists only $90 (4 business days or more) and $161 (less than 4 business days) and points to N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9. The state fee tiers are $45 / $90 / $161 at 10 and 4 business days, so call to confirm. The Township sheets still name a portable fire extinguisher, which P.L.2025, c.19 dropped from the state sale certificate in February 2025. The state directory email (holmdeltownship-nj.com) is older; the Township page uses dolsen@holmdel.gov.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations
other_items.detail: The CCO review confirms all construction permits are closed and all violations closed with penalties paid; work done without permits is cited and must be permitted.

other_items.label: Wells and septic
other_items.detail: Wells and septic systems must be maintained in good repair or properly abandoned as part of the CCO inspection.
